neighbours.label: examining something further or more closely: the follow-up step of an inquiry (investigate more closely, analysed further, look more carefully)
fire: Once the anomaly was flagged, the auditors went back to examine the accounts more closely.
The first scan looked normal, so the doctors ordered a second test to study the lesion further.
Any promising compound is then screened again and probed in greater depth by the chemists.
The committee agreed that the complaint deserved a closer look before any decision.
Detectives returned to the warehouse to search the back rooms more thoroughly.
If the pilot results hold up, the researchers plan to explore the effect further next year.
Telescopes on the ground can then follow up and observe the comet in more detail.
Her editor asked her to dig deeper into the company's links with the minister.
quiet: Once the anomaly was flagged, the auditors sent a short report to the board on Friday.
The first scan looked normal, so the doctors sent the patient home that evening.
Any promising compound is given a catalogue number and stored in the freezer.
The committee agreed that the complaint had been filed on the correct form.
Detectives arrived at the warehouse shortly after midnight with two dogs.
If the pilot results hold up, the researchers will publish them in a journal.
Telescopes on the ground were closed for the night because of heavy cloud.
Her editor told her the article about the minister would run on Sunday.

notes: Card: investigate, tested, executed, 'worth taking a closer look'; probe peaked on ' further', ' more', ' carefully'. Near misses keep the research topic but describe a first or finished step, not a follow-up.
